qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Municipal engineering specifications, certified utility standards, and vast global installed base of wastewater pumps and smart water infrastructure create customer switching inertia. However, empirical proof of moat is structurally absent: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~6.4% (FY21: 8.3%, FY22: 8.6%, FY23: 3.6%, FY24: 5.5%, FY25: 6.4%), consistently failing the 12% hurdle across the cycle. Dilutive mega-acquisitions (Sensus, Evoqua) continuously inflate the capital base with goodwill, while competitive RFP bidding and municipal budget caps prevent pricing power above inflation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Despite strong secular tailwinds in water infrastructure and treatment, Xylem fails the empirical proof-of-moat hurdle. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~6.4% (FY21: 8.3%, FY22: 8.6%, FY23: 3.6%, FY24: 5.5%, FY25: 6.4%) and 10-year historical ROIC has averaged sub-10%, well below the 12% threshold. Serial M&A (Sensus for $1.7B, Evoqua for $7.5B) has continuously diluted capital efficiency, while municipal tender dynamics restrict real pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial data confirms persistent sub-hurdle capital efficiency. GAAP ROIC: FY16 6.0%, FY17 8.0%, FY18 8.5%, FY19 6.7%, FY20 5.7%, FY21 8.3%, FY22 8.6%, FY23 3.6%, FY24 5.5%, FY25 6.4%. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~6.4%, far below the 12.0% hurdle. FY24 revenue of $8.56B converted to $1.01B operating income (11.8% margin) and $942M FCF. FY25 revenue of $9.04B delivered $1.22B operating income (13.5% margin) and $910M FCF. Despite solid FCF conversion and critical water installations, invested capital is heavily diluted by goodwill from serial M&A ($7.5B Evoqua merger closed May 2023). Municipal RFP procurement dynamics cap pricing power, leaving economic returns structurally mediocre across full business cycles.
